role: Actor or Actress (the word follows the character's pronouns, per HANDOFF)

facts.fact: The US Department of Labor describes the actor's work as attending auditions and casting calls, studying and rehearsing roles from scripts to learn lines, stunts and cues, performing the role, and promoting productions through interviews.

On a SAG-AFTRA film or television job the paid work besides shooting includes fittings and wardrobe and make-up tests, study of lines, publicity interviews, rehearsal and dialogue replacement (looping), each a section of the Codified Basic Agreement's day-performer schedule.

Feature films and scripted television made by AMPTP companies are covered by the SAG-AFTRA Codified Basic Agreement and Television Agreement, which also cover high-budget streaming (SVOD and AVOD) programs.

Independent films under $2 million are made under SAG-AFTRA's low-budget agreements; the Low Budget agreement requires an initial theatrical release, while the Ultra Low and Moderate Low agreements allow festivals, new media and theatrical release.
Commercials, industrials and public-service announcements are not made under the low-budget film agreements but under SAG-AFTRA's Commercials Contract.

A commercial performer is paid a session fee for the day's work and then use fees for each cycle the spot runs, by medium (streaming, digital, cable, broadcast, wild spot); the maximum period of use became 24 months under the 2025 contracts.
Video-game performance (voice and motion capture) is covered by SAG-AFTRA's Interactive Media Agreement, whose 2025 successor ended a nearly yearlong strike.
Stage work is Actors' Equity's jurisdiction: members of SAG-AFTRA and the other 4A's unions may not take theatrical employment without an Equity contract.
A union screen actor is an employee of the production, not an independent contractor, so the producer withholds payroll taxes.

Under the low-budget agreements a day is 8 hours, hours 8 to 12 are paid at time-and-a-half and hours past 12 at double time, and the producer pays only the days worked (no consecutive employment, except on overnight locations).
The Emmys bar voice-over performers and narrators from the lead, supporting and guest performer categories.

The 2026-30 SAG-AFTRA wage tables set these engagement forms, each with its own minimum: background actor, stand-in, day performer, three-day performer (television), weekly performer, major role performer, modified guest performer, modified deal performer, series regular (by episodes guaranteed) and term performer.

Television billing levels named in the 2026 agreement and the Actor Awards rules are co-star, guest star and series regular; a casting notice must seek the same level for a role in every market at once.
Term contracts carry lower beginner minimums for the first year: one rate for months 0 to 6 and a higher one for months 7 to 12.

Under the Codified Basic Agreement a "qualified professional performer", who must be given hiring preference for day and freelance roles within the preference zones, is someone employed as a motion picture performer at least once in the three years before the job.
The preference zones are 300 miles around Los Angeles and New York and 100 or 150 miles around the other listed production centres.
A day player engaged for a single day on a major-role part is paid at least day-player scale plus 10% under the 2026 agreement.
For series regulars the minimum payment for a studio to hold an option on the actor rises from 3 times to 5 times weekly scale for contracts from July 1, 2027.

A producer may not require union membership as a condition of employment until 30 days after the performer's first employment in the motion picture industry; after that the performer must join (pay initiation fee and dues) to keep working on union jobs.
Under the Taft-Hartley Act a signatory producer may hire a non-union performer who has a quality or skill essential to the role; the Moderate Low and Low Budget agreements apply these rules.
Producers may not charge a performer to see a casting notice or breakdown, or to upload a headshot, reel or self-tape, and may not favour performers who paid a casting service.

For a self-tape the producer must give the agent breakdowns and sides at least 48 hours (72 for a school-age minor) before the deadline, excluding weekends and holidays; a first self-tape is capped at 8 pages and later ones at 12; the actor need not memorize, is not paid for the tape, and cannot be required above 720p, to buy equipment, to tape nude or to do a stunt.
For series regular, recurring and major roles a producer must make good-faith efforts to let an actor invited to self-tape interview virtually or in person instead.
Recordings of interviews and auditions, including self-tapes, may be used only for casting and not made public without the actor's written consent.
An actor need not have an agent to get an audition on a SAG-AFTRA production.

An interview (a reading without camera or recording) is unpaid for the first hour; time beyond an hour is paid at straight time; if the studio has not told the actor in writing within three days that they got the role, they are deemed rejected.
A filmed audition or test pays nothing extra if the actor gets the part (unless kept waiting over an hour), and half a day's pay if they do not.
Producers send their casting director at least once a month to showcases run jointly by SAG-AFTRA and the Casting Society of America, or hold general interviews instead.
In California nobody may act as a talent agency (procuring work for an artist) without a licence from the Labor Commissioner; actors and actresses are "artists" under the Talent Agencies Act.
A California talent agency pays a $25 filing fee and a $225 annual licence fee ($50 per branch), and posts a $50,000 surety bond.
California sets no commission rate in statute: each agency files a fee schedule with the Labor Commissioner and its contract may not charge more than that schedule.
An agency must pay the actor their money, less commission, within 30 days of receiving it, and disputes with an agency go to the Labor Commissioner.
Every California agency contract must let either side end it if the actor, while available, gets no job or bona fide offer for more than four consecutive months.

Actors' Equity can be joined through an Equity contract, through "Open Access" (proof of professional stage work in its jurisdiction), or through a year's membership of a sibling union such as SAG-AFTRA with principal work or three days of background work.
Equity's initiation fee is $1,800, payable over up to three years; membership rights start after $600 is paid.
The 2026 TV/Theatrical agreement runs from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030, with 3% minimum increases each July 1.
Day performer minimum (film and television): $1,246 to June 30, 2026, then $1,283, $1,321, $1,361 and $1,402 from each July 1 of 2026 to 2029.
Weekly performer minimum: $4,456 a week from July 1, 2026 ($4,590, $4,728, $4,870 in the following years).
Background actor minimum: $231 a day from July 1, 2026 (special-ability background $10 more; stand-ins $270).
Television three-day performer minimum for a half-hour or one-hour show: $3,252 from July 1, 2026.
Major-role performers on network, pay-TV and high-budget streaming series get at least $7,057 per half-hour episode (5 days) or $11,290 per one-hour episode (8 days) from July 1, 2026.
Modified deal performer minimum is $25,551 and modified guest performer minimum $16,608 per episode from July 1, 2026.
Series regular minimums from July 1, 2026, per episode: half-hour $4,456 (13+ guaranteed) to $5,947 (6 guaranteed); one-hour $5,361 (13+) to $6,996 (6 guaranteed).
Term performers guaranteed 10-19 weeks get at least $3,826 a week and those guaranteed 20 weeks or more $3,184 a week from July 1, 2026.

Low-budget minimums from July 1, 2026: Ultra Low $257 a day; Moderate Low $449 a day or $1,560 a week; Low Budget $834 a day or $2,896 a week. They are set at 20%, 35% and 65% of Basic Agreement scale.
On the Micro-Budget agreement terms are fully negotiable, on the Student Film agreement actor pay is deferred, and on the Short Project agreement pay is negotiable.
On top of wages the producer pays pension and health contributions: 22% for principal performers and 21.5% for background from September 6, 2026.

Residuals on a theatrical film shown on free television are 6% of worldwide free-TV gross after a flat 40% deduction; pay-TV is 3.6% of distributor's gross; home video is 4.5% of the first $1 million and 5.4% thereafter, shared among the cast.

Commercials session fee (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027): $855.20 for an on-camera principal and $643.00 off-camera; wages rose 5%, 4% and 3% in the contract's three years; pension and health is 23.5% (19.95% for JPC authorizers).
A commercial that uses an actor's digital replica in place of an in-person performance pays 1.5 scale session fees per commercial.

The 2025 Interactive Media (video game) Agreement raised wages by a compounded 15.7% plus 3% each November 2025-2027, with health and retirement contributions at 17% and then 17.5% after October 31, 2026.
Actors' Equity members pay working dues of 2.5% of gross Equity earnings on top of $176 a year basic dues.
Median wage for actors in the US was $29.05 an hour in 2025, with 67,500 employed and about 6,300 openings projected for 2025-2035.
Low-budget producers who do not feed the cast owe a meal per diem of $70 a day, rising to $80 on July 1, 2028.
An actor called to a non-shooting day for safety or harassment-prevention training is paid four hours at no less than half the day-performer minimum.
The 2023 TV/Theatrical agreement followed a 118-day SAG-AFTRA strike; members approved the 2026 agreement.

To qualify for SAG-AFTRA Health Plan coverage an actor must earn at least $28,090 (2026 benefit year) in covered earnings in a four-quarter base period, or work 108 days; the minimum is $28,933 in 2027, $29,801 in 2028, $30,695 in 2029 and $31,616 in 2030; qualifying gives 12 months of coverage.
Health Plan premiums for an earned-eligibility participant alone are $375 a quarter in 2026 and $390 from January 1, 2027 ($531/$549 with one dependent, $747/$780 with two or more).

An actor who loses coverage can buy COBRA ($1,277 a month alone in 2026) or, with 12 or 20 Extended Career Credits and at least $22,300 of earnings (2027), Extended Career COBRA at $255 a month (2026).

Covered earnings are scale wages, session fees and residuals under SAG-AFTRA contracts, up to per-project ceilings (theatrical $232,000; one-hour TV episode $35,000; half-hour $25,000; interactive $125,000).
The SAG-Producers Pension Plan credits one year of pension service for each calendar year with at least $20,000 of covered earnings (since 2012); a year under $10,000 is a one-year break in service.
An actor is vested in the pension after 10 pension credits, or 5 credits without a permanent break plus the activity test, or on reaching normal retirement age.
The regular pension starts at 65 with ten credits; an early pension can start from 55, reduced by a quarter of one percent for each month under 65.
Because of the 2023 strike, 2023 is not counted toward breaks in service for TV/Theatrical participants who worked 2019-2023.
The SAG-Producers Pension Plan and the AFTRA Retirement Fund are to merge into one plan, targeted for January 1, 2028.

SAG-AFTRA applies a rule it calls Global Rule One to members' work abroad: the Actor Awards treat a production made outside the US that employs a member as eligible only where SAG-AFTRA finds the employment covered by a SAG-AFTRA contract under Global Rule 1.
An Equity member two years behind on dues, without inactive status, loses membership and can rejoin only through Open Access.
Every theatrical feature ends with a cast card naming performer and role; with a cast of 50 or fewer every performer is credited, otherwise at least 50 are listed.
Billing (placement, size and description) is whatever the actor's individual contract negotiates, and the producer must honour it and forbid distributors from changing it.

A dispute over whether agreed screen credit was given goes to a single arbitrator; a day performer's damages are a day's pay, a weekly freelance performer's a week's pay, and claims must be filed within one year of first release or broadcast.
Only roles credited in a film's legal billing, performed by humans with their consent, are eligible for the Academy's acting awards; uncredited performances are not.

The Actor Awards' cast-in-a-motion-picture award goes to actors with single-card main-title billing; in television ensembles a series regular or a guest star in a majority of episodes is included and a co-star is not.

The Academy's four acting Oscars are Actor and Actress in a Leading Role and Actor and Actress in a Supporting Role; the Actors Branch nominates five in each, and all active and life members vote the winners.
A performance whose dialogue is entirely dubbed by another actor is not eligible for an Oscar; the branch decides individually whether a role is leading or supporting.
For the 99th Oscars a film must start a seven-day theatrical qualifying run between January 1 and December 31, 2026 in one of six US metro areas.

The Actor Awards presented by SAG-AFTRA cover films over 60 minutes and primetime TV first shown in 2026; nominating committees are drawn by random sample of paid-up members over 18, and all active members in good standing in the US and Canada vote the winners; the 33rd ceremony is February 28, 2027.
The Emmys give lead, supporting and guest awards for actors and actresses separately in comedy, drama and limited series; guest performers appear in under 50% of episodes and need 5% of screen time.

A producer may not use its own casting or production staff as performers on the same picture without SAG-AFTRA's consent, except performer/directors, performer/writers and performer/producers engaged in writing as such before principal photography begins.
Breaking that rule costs the producer liquidated damages of $500 per day performer, $600 per three-day performer and $800 per freelance performer.
Pay for directing, writing or producing does not count toward an actor's SAG-AFTRA Health Plan eligibility.
California's Talent Agencies Act counts directors and writers as "artists" alongside actors and actresses, so the same licensing rules govern an agent who finds an actor work as a director or writer.

topics.topic: Time and money of a project

facts.fact: Budget caps decide the low-budget agreement: Micro-Budget up to $20,000, Student Film $35,000, Short Project $50,000 (40 minutes or less), Ultra Low $300,000, Moderate Low $700,000, Low Budget $2,000,000.
A production that meets the diversity-in-casting test can raise the Moderate Low cap to $950,000 and the Low Budget cap to $3,000,000.
A producer should start the SAG-AFTRA signatory process 4 to 6 weeks before the cast starts work.
Employers report an actor's earnings to the plans within 30 days of paying them, and the earnings usually show on the actor's account 6 to 8 weeks after the work.
A modified deal or modified guest performer's overall production period may not exceed 180 calendar days for contracts from September 1, 2026.
Day performers on theatrical films earning $10,000 a day may have up to two prepaid looping days in their contract.
The SAG-AFTRA agreement commits producers to non-discrimination in hiring and treating performers on the basis of sex, age, sexual orientation and gender identity, among others.
Producers must cast "so that, for example, the American scene shall be portrayed realistically" and make every effort to include women and performers aged 40 or over.

Producers may not ask a performer's age before hiring except for a minor or where it is a bona fide occupational qualification for the role, and breakdowns state that non-descript roles accept all performers regardless of age, sex or gender identity.
When a stunt double doubles a role identifiable as female, stunt coordinators should cast a double of the same sex.
California bars a licensed talent agency from refusing to represent an artist because of sex.

Low-budget producers earn a higher budget cap if at least half the speaking roles and days of employment go to women, performers over 60, performers with disabilities and people of colour, and at least 20% of days to people of colour.
Producers must use best efforts to let performers give their pronouns and show them on deal memos, cast lists and call sheets.
The Oscars keep separate actor and actress categories (leading and supporting).
The Actor Awards split individual awards into Male Actor and Female Actor categories.
The Emmys keep separate actor and actress categories with the same number of nominations in each pair; a nominee may ask for "Performer" on the certificate instead of Actor or Actress.
The Berlinale made its acting prizes gender-neutral from 2021 (announced August 24, 2020): a Silver Bear for Best Leading Performance and for Best Supporting Performance.
The Gotham Awards replaced Best Actor and Best Actress with gender-neutral Outstanding Lead and Supporting Performance from 2021 (announced August 5, 2021).
Under the SAG-AFTRA agreement a minor is a performer under 18, unless they have finished compulsory schooling, are married, serve in the armed forces or are emancipated.
A minor guaranteed three or more consecutive days on a school day must be given a teacher from the first day.
A chaperone is required for minors up to 16 under the 2026 agreement (it was under 14), and a minor's digital replica may never be shown nude or in simulated sex.
In California every minor from 15 days to 18 years working in entertainment needs an entertainment work permit from the Labor Commissioner, and the employer needs a permit to employ minors.
California minors may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 a week, between 5 a.m. and 10 p.m. (12:30 a.m. before a non-school day), with 12 hours between dismissal and the next call.

California work time by age: infants (15 days to 6 months) 20 minutes; 6 months to 2 years 2 hours; 2 to 6 years 3 hours; 6 to 9 years 4 hours on a school day; 9 to 16 years 5 hours; 16 to 18 years 6 hours; school-age minors also get 3 hours of schooling a day.
One studio teacher is required for every 10 minors aged 6 months to 16 when school is in session (20 on weekends and holidays), and a parent or guardian must be present.
Before a California permit is issued to a minor aged 14 to 17, the minor (with a parent) must complete sexual-harassment-prevention training.
A minor's contract with a licensed talent agency, once approved by the superior court where the minor lives or works, cannot be disaffirmed by the minor later.

Under California's Coogan law (Family Code 6752) the employer must set aside 15% of a minor's gross earnings into a trust (Coogan account), whether or not the court approves the contract; background and extra work is exempt.

The trustee gives the employer the trust statement within 10 business days of the start of work, the employer deposits within 15 business days of receiving it, and after 180 days without it the money goes to The Actors' Fund of America as trustee.

In New York a child performer needs a Department of Labor permit before work, and parents must open a trust receiving at least 15% of gross earnings (a trust company must take over above $250,000); a temporary permit gives 15 days to open it.
New York child performers get a certified teacher averaging at least three hours a school day and may not go more than ten consecutive school days without instruction.
Actors' Equity has members under 18 (juvenile performers), who may take Juvenile Withdrawal to do non-union school or community theatre.
Actor Awards nominating committee members must be over 18.
In California professional actors, unlike other minors, are exempt from minimum-wage and overtime rules.

note:
Read 2026-10-31. The US screen actor's working rules as the agreements and governments state them. Documents and their dates in force: the AMPTP's 2026-30 SAG-AFTRA wage tables (printed 2026-05-27; rates for 7/1/25-6/30/30) and the fully executed 2026 Memorandum of Agreement (2026-05-27; term July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030), both from the AMPTP, the producers' bargaining party, so primary; the 2014 Codified Basic Agreement (the last codified text the AMPTP posts; its sections on union security, preference of employment, screen credits, non-discrimination, production staff, casting, minors, interviews, auditions and residual percentages are cited as the base text, and the 2017, 2020, 2023 and 2026 MOAs were not read in full for later changes to those sections, except the 2023 MOA's new self-tape rules and the 2026 MOA's casting changes); the SAG-AFTRA Health Plan's pages (minimums and premiums adopted 2026-08-27, in force 2027-01-01); the SAG-Producers Pension Plan's SPD (July 1, 2019) and its amendments 2 and 3 (amendment 3 dated July 2026, which changed benefit forms and break-in-service restoration, not the credit thresholds); Actors' Equity's join, dues and young performers pages (undated); O*NET 27-2011.00 (BLS 2025 wages, 2025-2035 projections); California DLSE's Laws Relating to Talent Agencies (Rev. 1/25) and talent agency licence page (October 2024); California DLSE's Child Labor Laws pamphlet (2013; the hours and teacher rules cite 8 CCR 11750-11765 and Labor Code 1308.5-1308.8, not re-checked against a later text because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a Cloudflare check); AB 533's chaptered text (2013) for Family Code 6752 (later amendments, if any, not checked for the same reason; The Actors' Fund of America is now called the Entertainment Community Fund, which SAGindie's page lists, but the statute text read uses the old name); New York DOL's child performer page (undated); the 99th Academy Awards rules (copy of the Academy's PDF held by Costa Rica's Centro de Cine, kind secondary, because oscars.org refuses this egress with 403); the Actor Awards' 33rd eligibility, categories and rules pages; the Television Academy's 78th Emmy rules (version 4, 2026-04-07); the Berlinale's release of 2020-08-24 and The Gotham's of 2021-08-05; the Joint Policy Committee's 2025 Commercials Contracts alert (2025-04-28) and its 4/1/26-3/31/27 rate sheet (the JPC is the advertisers' bargaining party, so primary).
Secondary, each quoting the primary named in its quotes: SAGindie's signatory page (rendered with an honest browser because its content loads by script), its 2023 and 2026 contract notices and FAQ (SAGindie is a division of Film-Raderie, not SAG-AFTRA, so marked secondary); the Association of Talent Agents' excerpted summary of the 2026 tentative agreement (2026-05-11; its points on fittings, major role, MDP period, options, chaperones, pronouns, prepaid looping, training calls and the plan merger were not re-found in the MOA by me and rest on the ATA's summary); Frankfurt Kurnit's summary of the 2025 Interactive Media Agreement (the IMA's own text and rate sheet are on sagaftra.org, refused).
Readings made: the ladder's order of engagement forms is my reading of the wage tables (they list the forms; they do not call them a ladder), and the billing list adds "recurring" from the 2026 MOA's casting provision; the low-budget percentages of Basic Agreement scale are SAGindie's statement; the commercials session fee is the year-2 sheet's "Session" row, principal on camera and off camera columns; "Day performer minimum (film and television)" joins the Codified Basic Agreement and Television Agreement rows, which are equal.
Not found, with what was tried: SAG-AFTRA's own pages and PDFs (membership routes and eligibility, the initiation fee and dues, Global Rule One's text, the agency regulations and Rule 16(g), the self-tape guidelines page, the young performers page, the Commercials and Interactive rate sheets) because sagaftra.org answers this egress with a captcha (403); archive.org's availability API shows snapshots of steps-join (2025-05-21), membership-costs (2025-05-13), contracts-industry-resources/global-rule-one (2025-06-02), membership-benefits/young-performers (2025-05-29), professional-representatives/info-agents-members (2024-06-24) and join (2024-06-24), but web.archive.org reset every raw fetch (code 000, ws_closed_mid_exchange) from 05:17 to the end of this run, so none was read. Hence not stated here: SAG-AFTRA's initiation fee, base and work dues, the age it admits members at, the 10% commission cap of its agency regulations, and the Association of Talent Agents' franchise terms. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and OEWS 27-2011 pages (percentiles, entry education) are refused by Akamai (403) and the BLS API returned its daily threshold; their snapshots (OOH 2026-10-20, OEWS 2025-03-27) were not readable for the same archive reason, so only O*NET's median, employment and projection are given. Casting Society of America's site is behind Cloudflare. The Golden Globes' site gives a captcha and BAFTA's and Film Independent's (Spirit Awards) a Cloudflare check, so their acting-category rules are not stated; no archive snapshot of their rules pages was found by the availability API. Training paths: Juilliard's pages give a Cloudflare check and NYU Tisch's did not answer, so no school's catalogue is cited. How long a rise from background to series regular typically takes: no source measuring it was found. Age-limited roles: no agreement or law read states one; playing age is not a rule in any source read, and the only age rules found are the minors' rules, the bar on pre-employment age questions, and the 40-plus and 60-plus inclusion provisions.
